title: Reverse Segments Between Zero Nodes
description:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list of integers where nodes with value `0` act as fixed delimiters, reverse every maximal contiguous segment of non-zero nodes in-place while keeping every `0` node at its exact original position.

Segments at the very start of the list (before the first `0`), at the very end (after the last `0`), or when there are no `0` nodes at all are also reversed. Return the head of the modified linked list in `O(n)` time and `O(1)` extra space.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 10^4].
hints: Use a sentinel `dummy` node and a `prev` pointer that always points immediately before the current position.

When `prev.next.val == 0`, simply advance `prev`; otherwise reverse nodes starting at `prev.next` until encountering `0` or `null`, stitch the reversed segment back between `prev` and the delimiter, and move `prev` to the segment's new tail.

examples.explanation: Zeros stay fixed while [1, 2] reverses to [2, 1] and [3, 4, 5] reverses to [5, 4, 3].
With no zeros, the whole list [7, 8, 9] reverses to [9, 8, 7].
